# The kitchen — cook.html, the recipe library, and the cooking files

Load this when the task is about meal planning, recipes, shopping lists, or
the Cook page.

## What exists

**The page: `brain/cook.html`** (GENERATED by `brain/tools/cook.py`; it also
rides every `build.py` run). Five tabs:

- **Week** — tonight's dinner as the hero (Cook / Recipe / Cooked it), a
  7-day dinner grid for this week and next, "+ plan" on every day, a
  neutral balance line (n planned · n veg · n fish · median minutes), and
  "Build shopping list" per week. **Leftovers:** the empty day after a
  meal-prep dish shows a one-tap "↻ leftovers of X" ghost (the hero
  offers it too when tonight is empty). A leftovers entry is the same
  recipe id with `(leftovers)` in plan.md — it renders with the ↻ mark,
  is skipped by the shopping builder, and stays out of the cooking-time
  median.
- **Find** — search over all 6,328 recipes (title + ingredient), filter
  chips: Quick, ≤5 ingredients, High protein, Dorm-friendly, From my
  pantry (ranked by fewest missing), Veg, Saved, plus book and kind.
  Cards show photos where the book has them (photo-first, books
  interleaved). Click → drawer with photo, headnote, ingredients
  (pantry-matched ones marked "have"), method, and the actions: Plan it /
  Cook mode / Cooked it / Save.

  The facet flags are derived at index time (`_analyse_method` +
  `_is_protein` in cook.py), honest heuristics, not nutrition data:
  **Quick** = total time ≤30 min. Some books state only active time
  ("Active: 30 mins. Total: 4 hrs.") — the parser reads the stated total
  out of the recipe text (434 recipes) and it always wins; with only an
  active time, an hours/overnight mention in the method disqualifies;
  with no time at all, ≤3 steps and ≤8 non-staple ingredients. Cards and
  the drawer show the total ("30 min active, 4 h total"). **≤5 ingredients** = ≤5 beyond the cupboard —
  the `CUPBOARD` set in cook.py (basics, dried spices, vinegars, soy
  sauce, mustard, honey, baking essentials) doesn't count, matched
  exact-or-ends-with so "mustard greens", "peanut butter" and specialty
  flours still count as real ingredients. **High protein** = a real protein anchor (meat, fish, eggs,
  tofu, paneer, legumes) in the list — stocks, sauces and pastes don't
  count, and desserts never qualify (a dessert-title detector catches
  flans and custards that technique-chaptered books hide from the
  category rules; a savory veto keeps salmon mousse savory).
  **Dorm-friendly** = a real weeknight MEAL on her campus setup (one
  large + one small burner): no oven/broiler/grill, no
  blender/processor/mixer, at most two stovetop vessels, and never a
  drink, dip, sauce or dessert (`NOT_A_MEAL`). **Meal-prep** = keeps
  and reheats: soups/stews, legumes and grains by nature; anything else
  when the book itself says so (leftovers/reheat/keeps/freezes) or it
  serves 6+; never salads or egg dishes. There is deliberately no
  "healthy" badge — the books carry no nutrition data; healthy is
  composed from Veg + High protein + Quick, and a food-tracking app does that job.

  **Shop swaps** — `SWAPS` in cook.py maps ~60 American-cookbook
  ingredients a medium French supermarket won't reliably stock (kale,
  buttermilk, tomatillos, gochujang…) to what to buy instead, French
  shelf names included. The drawer shows the swap under the ingredient;
  the shopping list shows it on the item ("not there? → …"). Extend the dict when the owner reports a miss, and use it when
  drafting anything shopping-related.
- **Shopping** — aisle-grouped tickable list built from a week's plan,
  consolidated across recipes with quantities shown; her own additions
  survive rebuilds, as do ticks; pantry items fold into "Probably have";
  "copy the list" for a plain-text version.
- **Pantry** — Staples (assumed by the matcher) and Fresh right now, as
  add/remove chips. "Clear" on Fresh for a house move. Also **the
  kitchen switch**: Full kitchen / Dorm (two burners, no oven), stored
  under `## Kitchen` in pantry.md. Dorm mode gates tonight-suggestions
  to dorm-friendly recipes and pre-selects the Dorm chip in Find — flip
  it when she moves between campus and a family house.
- **Cooked** — the log (written by "Cooked it"), star to Save; saved
  recipes float up in tonight-suggestions and get their own Find filter.
- **Cook mode** — full-screen one-step-at-a-time method, big type, screen
  wake lock, from the hero or any recipe drawer.

**The library: `brain/recipes-library/`** — 6,328 recipes extracted from
her own 27 cookbooks (markdown per book, photos for 18 of them,
`pantry_db.json` with normalised ingredients). Static data, gitignored,
copied from `~/Downloads/extracted_recipes/` on 2026-08-29 and re-synced
2026-08-31 (added The Wok, 226 recipes; the same re-extraction also fixed
the NYT, King Arthur and RecipeTin books). Treat it as read-only;
`cook.py --reindex` rebuilds the derived index if it ever changes.

**Her own recipes: `brain/cooking/my-recipes.md`** — things she found, was
told, or worked out, in the same shape as a book file (`## Title`, optional
`<sub>chapter</sub>`, a headnote, `Serves N · Total: N minutes`,
`**Ingredients**` list, `**Method**` with `**1.**` steps). `_mine_records()`
in cook.py turns it into index records, so it searches, filters, plans and
shops exactly like the 27 books — book name "My recipes". Unlike the
library it COMMITS: it is hers, and it survives a re-extraction. Ingredient
names are normalised by `_norm_ing` (quantities and prep stripped) for the
pantry matcher. When she sends recipes to add, append them here — never
into `recipes-library/`, which is generated and gitignored. Keep calorie
counts OUT even when the source is full of them (see "Goals" below).

**Her state: `brain/cooking/`** — the state files the page writes and
she may edit by hand. Formats matter (`cook.py` parses them):

- `plan.md` — `## Week of YYYY-MM-DD` (a Monday), then
  `- Mon: Title {id: book_file/slug}` lines. The id links back to the
  library; a line without one is fine (shows as text only).
- `shopping.md` — aisle `## ` sections of `- [ ] item — detail` lines,
  plus `## Your additions` (hers, kept across rebuilds) and
  `## Probably have (from the pantry)`.
- `pantry.md` — `## Staples` and `## Fresh right now`, one item per line.
- `cooked.md` — `## Log` (`- date — Title {id} — note`) and `## Saved`.
- `taste.md` — `## Love`, `## Avoid`, `## Bored of`, one phrase per line.
  HERS: whole phrases ("anything with lemon", "no offal"), matched on any
  word of 4+ letters against the title and ingredients. `Avoid` is a hard
  veto in the planner, `Bored of` is a penalty. Never write a line here she
  did not say — an invented preference is worse than an empty file.
- `basket.md` — `- item — N · last YYYY-MM-DD`, counted up from the
  receipts she uploads. Generated, but she prunes it from the Pantry tab.

## Plan my week

The Week tab's **Plan my week** button (N meals, default 5) proposes a set
of dinners chosen to SHARE ingredients, then shows how many distinct things
the week needs and which ones repeat. Nothing is written until she presses
**Use these**, which fills only the empty days; Shuffle takes the next-best
set and Swap replaces one row.

All of it runs in the page from `cook-data.json` — no Claude call, no cost,
so she can press it as often as she likes. The moving parts, all in
`cook.py`'s template:

- `planCandidates()` — the gate and the per-recipe score. A dinner needs a
  protein or to be a veg dish, 5+ ingredients, and 4+ things to actually
  buy; without that last one the optimiser picks scrambled eggs and aioli,
  because they add nothing to the list. Score = saved + taste hits + basket
  coverage + protein/quick/veg + pantry coverage, minus anything cooked in
  the last 21 days.
- `greedyFrom()` — picks an opener, then repeatedly takes whatever scores
  best on `base*0.55 + shared*1.5 - fresh*0.85 - repeats*1.4`. Both halves
  are needed: reward sharing alone and it picks sprawling dishes that touch
  everything, penalise new ingredients alone and it picks the smallest
  recipe in the book. Near-duplicate titles ("Cheese Tart" / "Cheese Tarts")
  are collapsed by `titleKey`, and no category may exceed `max(2, n/3)`.
- `planWeek()` — the opener decides most of the result, so it runs 14 of
  them and keeps the set with the best `taste - 2.6 × distinct items`.

Measured on the real index, 5 meals: **14 distinct things to buy against 30
with the overlap term off.** If she says the weeks are samey, raise the
category cap; if the shopping list is too long, raise the `2.6`.

**Server:** `/api/cook/*` in `serve.py` dispatches to `cook.api()`; every
write rewrites the markdown and rebuilds only cook.html (fast — the recipe
index is cached in `brain/cooking/.recipes.json`). The page's data file is
`brain/cook-data.json` (~2 MB, regenerated only when the index changes).

## Telegram

Two kitchen paths in the bridge (`telegram_bridge.py`):

- **A photo** — downloaded to `brain/files/telegram/` (gitignored) and
  queued with the path attached. No caption, or a caption with
  receipt/ticket/caisse/courses/groceries → the receipt workflow: Read
  the image, add purchases to pantry Fresh (short generic names), **fold
  the same list into the basket** with
  `cook.api("basketadd", {"items": [...]})` so the week planner learns
  what she actually buys (till lines go in raw — `_norm_basket` strips
  the multipliers, pack sizes and prices), tick
  matching shopping.md items, rebuild via cook.py, and put what she
  bought + 2–3 unlocked dinners in the Outcome. **Never log food as
  eaten — a food tracker handles eating; a receipt only stocks the kitchen.** Any
  other caption is her instruction for that photo.
- **`cook: chicken, tomatoes`** — answered instantly by the bridge
  itself from the recipe index (her listed items + pantry, ≤1 missing,
  dorm-gated when the kitchen says dorm). Mechanical — no Claude call,
  no cost.

## How Claude uses it

- **/today** — read `brain/cooking/plan.md`; if tonight has a dinner, the
  plan can mention it (and any defrost-ahead prep). If the week is empty by
  Sunday, planning 2–3 dinners is a fair non-computer suggestion — cooking
  is on her enjoys-list and serves the health front.
- **Goals, without moralizing.** She's trying to cook healthier and
  simpler (insulin resistance context lives in about-me). The page only
  counts (veg/fish/minutes) and never advises; keep it that way. Never
  quote health numbers. A food tracker stays the food tracker — the Cook page
  plans, it does not track nutrition.
- **Suggestions logic** (in the page): saved recipes, pantry coverage,
  ≤45 min, mains over sides. If she says the suggestions are off, tune
  `suggestions()` in cook.py.
- **She asks "what can I make with X"** — answer from
  `python3 brain/recipes-library/pantry.py X ...` (the original CLI
  matcher, same data), or point her at Find → From my pantry.
- **Never mark a plan entry cooked** unless she said so; "Cooked it" on
  the page is her word.

## Maintenance

- After editing anything under `brain/cooking/`, run
  `python3 brain/tools/cook.py` (or the full build).
- `cook.html`, `cook-data.json`, `recipes-library/`, and the index cache
  are gitignored on purpose — static or derived, they'd only churn
  history. The four markdown state files DO commit.
- serve.py holds the `/api/cook/` routes; a serve.py edit needs the manual
  server restart (see the memory note / operations reference).
